newsitem.title: USA: Apple sets $250 mln in charges, more layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Apple sets $250 mln in charges, more layoffs.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc said Friday it will cut 4,100 permanent, temporary and contract jobs -- or 31 percent of its workforce -- to adjust its expenses to rapidly falling revenues.
To pay for the job cuts, Apple will take a total of $250 million in charges in the next three quarters, starting with a $155 million charge in the fiscal second quarter, ending March.
Apple said it expects revenue for the second quarter to plunge about 22 percent to $1.6 to $1.7 billion, down from $2.2 billion in the same quarter a year ago.

To continue to cut expenses, Apple will drop several product lines, but its Newton handheld computer will remain intact for now, Apple executives said. Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio said he foresees no more senior management departures, despite the company's organizational restructuring.
Apple also has enough adequate cash for now to cover the expense of the layoffs, Apple's chief financial officer Fred Anderson said.
